Rashi on Nazir 24b:2:1.hebrew: היא מנא לה - הא בהמה? הא קיימא לן: מה שקנתה אשה קנה בעלה:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:2:1.english: She, from where does she have [it] - [From where does she have] this animal? Behold, we maintain: Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:2:2.hebrew: שקמצתה מעיסתה - כגון דהשרה לה מזונות על ידי שליש. ותנן בפרק אע"פ (כתובות סד:) דלא יפחות לה בשבוע משני קבין חיטין, והלכה זו וקיפחה ממזונותיה על יד, עד שלקחה בהן בהמה זו:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:2:2.english: Where she saved from her dough - For example, where he provided her sustenance through a trustee. And we learned in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 64b) that he may not give her less than two kav of wheat a week; and this [woman] went and skimped on her food little by little, until she purchased this animal with [the savings].

Rashi on Nazir 24b:2:3.hebrew: איבעית אימא דאקני לה אחר - דאי קימצתה מעיסתה, אמרינן נמי: מה שקמצתה אשה קנה בעלה:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:2:3.english: And if you wish, say that another [person] transferred [it] to her - For if [it were because] she saved from her dough, we could also say: Whatever a woman saves, her husband acquires.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:3:1.hebrew: א"ל שמואל לאבוה בר איהי כו' שלה - [הא דאמרן] במשנתנו, דאין טעונים לחם:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:3:1.english: Shmuel said to Avuh bar Ihi, etc., hers - [That which we said] in our mishna, that they do not require bread.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:4:1.english: [If] he shaved - During the days of his naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:4:2.hebrew: או שגילחוהו הקרובים - בתוך ימי נזירותו. או שמיחה — אע"פ שלא נתגלח, בטלה נזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:4:2.english: Or if the relatives shaved him - During the days of his naziriteship. Or if he objected — even though he was not shaved, [his] naziriteship is canceled.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:5:1.hebrew: ואם היו לו מעות סתומין יפלו לנדבה - ויביאו מהן עולות לקיץ המזבח, דאין חוששין לדמי חטאת שבהן כדלקמן, שהלכה היא בנזיר כך:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:5:1.english: And if he had unallocated funds, they shall fall for a gift-offering - And they shall bring from them burnt-offerings for the summer fruit of the Altar, as we do not take into account the sin-offering money in them, as [explained] below, for such is the halakhah regarding a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:6:1.english: One who separates money for his naziriteship - And they were unspecified [funds].

Rashi on Nazir 24b:6:2.hebrew: לא נהנין ולא מועלין בהן מפני שהן ראוין להביא בכולן שלמים - דבכל מעה ומעה שלהן יכול להביא בהן שלמים, ובשלמים אמרינן (מעילה דף ו:) דליכא מעילה לפני זריקת דמים:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:6:2.english: One may not derive benefit, nor is [one] liable for misuse with them, because they are fit to bring peace-offerings with all of them - For with each and every coin of theirs he can bring peace-offerings, and regarding peace-offerings we say (Me'ila 6b) that there is no [liability for] misuse prior to the sprinkling of the blood.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:7:1.hebrew: מעות מפורשין דמי עולה יביאו עולה - וה"ה דהוה ליה למיתני, דדמי חטאת ילכו לים המלח:
Rashi on Nazir 24b:7:1.english: Allocated funds, the money for a burnt-offering shall be brought as a burnt-offering - And the same law applies, that it could have taught that the money for a sin-offering shall go to the Dead Sea.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:8:1.hebrew: שלאחר כפרה - שאם הפריש בהמתו ואבדה, או מעות ואבדן, והפריש אחרים תחתיהן, ואח"כ נמצאו: חטאת או דמי חטאת — יוליך לים המלח; והעולה — תקרב עולה; והשלמים — לשלמים, ונאכלים ליום אחד, ואינן טעונין לחם — דסברא הוא כו':
Rashi on Nazir 24b:8:1.english: [That which is] after atonement - That if he designated his animal and it was lost, or money and he lost it, and he designated others in their place, and afterward they were found: [the] sin-offering or the money of [the] sin-offering shall be taken to the Dead Sea; and the burnt-offering shall be sacrificed as a burnt-offering; and the peace-offering [shall be sacrificed] as a peace-offering, and is eaten for one day, and does not require bread — for it is [based on] logical reasoning, etc.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:9:1.english: And is there nothing else - Other than these four rams that do not require bread?

Rashi on Nazir 24b:9:2.hebrew: והא איכא - דתני לוי במתני', דאמר במס' מנחות (מח:) ובתוספתא דנזיר (פ"ד):
Rashi on Nazir 24b:9:2.english: But isn’t there - [That] which Levi taught in a baraita, as is stated in Tractate Menachot (48b) and in the Tosefta of Nazir (ch. 4):

Rashi on Nazir 24b:9:3.english: And all the other peace-offerings of a nazirite - Earlier [in the baraita], it is dealing with peace-offerings.

Rashi on Nazir 24b:9:4.english: That were slaughtered not in accordance with their mitzva - For their mitzva is to bring [a ram] in its second year for the sake of the peace-offering of a nazirite.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:11:1.hebrew: היו לו מעות סתומים - הכי גרסינן בספרים: "והיו לו", ומשמע דקאי אמפריש מעות לנזירותו דמסכת מעילה, ולא אמתני' [דהכא] ד"היו לה מעות סתומים". ונראה דלכך לא קשיא ליה אמתני' [דהכא], משום דאיכא לאוקומי דאמר "לנזירות", ולכך יפלו לנדבה — דאי בעי, מייתי בכולן עולה. אבל אמתני' דהתם קשיא ליה, דע"כ מיירי היכא דאמר "לקרבנות נזירותי", דאם לא כן, אמאי תנא "מעות סתומות"? והא בסתומין איירי בהך דינא (דלעיל)! אבל במתני' — דעד השתא איירי בבהמות, ועתה התחיל לשנות דין דמעות סתומין — ולהכי פריך אהא דהתם: "סתומים יפלו":
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:11:1.english: "If he had unallocated funds" - This is the reading in the texts: "And if he had" [vehayu lo], and it implies that [the Gemara] refers to [the Mishnah regarding] "One who sets aside funds for his naziriteship..." in tractate Meilah, and not to our Mishnah [here], which [states]: "If she had unallocated funds" [hayu lah]. And it appears that the reason this was not difficult to [the Gemara] from our Mishnah [here] is that it can be established that he said [merely], "[These funds are] for naziriteship," and therefore they shall fall to a gift offering — for if he wished, he could bring all of them as a burnt-offering. But from the Mishnah there [in Meilah], it was difficult to it, for perforce [that Mishnah] deals with a case where he said, "[These funds are] for the offerings of my naziriteship" — for if not so, why did [the tanna] teach "unallocated funds"? Isn't it already dealing with unallocated [funds] in that [first] ruling (above)? However, in the Mishnah [here], since until now it was dealing with animals, and only now began to teach the ruling of unallocated funds — therefore [the Gemara] objects to that which [was taught] there [in Meilah]: "Unallocated [funds] shall fall [to a gift offering]."

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:11:2.hebrew: הגה"ה: יפלו לנדבה, והלא דמי חטאת מעורבין בהן - ואיך יפלו לנדבה? והוא הדין דהוה מצי לאותובי: והלא דמי שלמים מעורבין שאינן כליל, ואיך יפלו לנדבה לעולת קיץ למזבח דהוי כולה כליל?! אלא דעדיפא פריך — מחטאת, שאינו כלל בר הקרבה לאחר המיתה, אלא לים המלח אזיל. וא"ת: [וליתני] מפני שראוין להביא בכולן [עולה], כדאמר לעיל: מפני שראוין להביא בכולן שלמים? וי"ל: דהכא, משום כשהוא חי שייך למימר מימליך; אבל כשמת לא שייך למימר מימליך, והרי הם כתחילת הפרשה, והרי הם כמפורשים גם לחטאת. ועי"ל: דהא דאמר שיכול לשנות להביאן כולן לשלמים, היינו דווקא היכא דאמר: "אלו מעות לנזירותי", דמשמע: אם ארצה אביא בשליש עולה ובשליש חטאת ובשליש שלמים, או אם ארצה אעשה מכולן חטאת או מכולן שלמים — ד"לנזירות" משמע שפיר למקצת נזירותו; אבל היכא דמת והיו לו מעות סתומין דיפלו לנדבה, דאיירי בהפריש מעות ואמר: "מעות הללו לקרבנות נזירותי", לא יוכל להביא בכולן קרבן אחד, דהא "קרבנות" קאמר, הילכך יש במעות הללו דמי חטאת; לכך פריך: איך יהא בכולן נדבה, והלא דמי חטאת מעורבין בהן?! ובזה מתיישב לשון מתני' דמעילה (דף יא.): "המפריש [מעות] לנזירות אין מועלין בהן, מפני שראויין לבא בכולן שלמים" [ומיירי מתני'], ובתר הכי תני: "מת והיו לו מעות סתומין" — והא בסתומין איירינן, והכי איבעי ליה למימר: "מת יפלו לנדבה"?! אלא הכא [קא מיירי] דאמר דוקא "לנזירותי", דאז יכול להביא בכולן אחד מקרבנותיו, דמשמע אכל קרבנותיו קאמר; ולכך קתני בסיפא: "מת והיו לו מעות סתומין", ואפילו נמי אמר: "אלו לקרבנות נזירותי", כולן יפלו לנדבה. וכן מוכח מההוא (דלרבא) [דלקמן] (דף כו:): "אלו לחטאתי והשאר לשאר נזירותי", ומת — דמי חטאת ילכו לים המלח, והשאר יביא בחציו עולה ובחציו שלמים; ומשמע משום דאמר "השאר לשאר נזירות" דחשבינן ליה כאומר "לקרבנות נזירותי", אבל אמר "והשאר לנזירותי", ולא "לשאר" — מכולן יעשה מהם עולה או שלמים מכולן. כך פר"י [ הגה"ה]:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:11:2.english: [Gloss:] "They are allocated for gift offerings. But is not money for a sin-offering mingled with them?" - And how could they be allocated for gift offerings? And the same applies that [the Gemara] could have objected: But is not money for a peace-offering mingled [with them], which is not entirely consumed [on the altar], and how could they be allocated for gift offerings for the "summer fruit" burnt-offering for the altar, which is entirely consumed? Rather, it raised a stronger objection from the sin-offering, which is not eligible for sacrifice at all after [the owner's] death, but rather goes to the Dead Sea. And if you should say: [Let it teach:] "Because they are fit to bring a [burnt-offering] with all of them," just as [the Mishnah] stated above: "Because they are fit to bring a peace-offering with all of them"? And one can say: Here, because when he is alive, it is applicable to say that he may change his mind; but when he died, it is not applicable to say that he may change his mind, and they remain as at the initial designation, and they are as if explicitly designated also for a sin-offering. And furthermore, one can say: That which was said that he can change [his mind] to bring them all for peace-offerings, that is specifically where he said, "These coins are for my naziriteship," which implies: If I wish, I will bring a third as a burnt-offering, a third as a sin-offering, and a third as a peace-offering; or if I wish, I will make all of them a sin-offering or all of them a peace-offering — for "for my naziriteship" can well mean for part of his naziriteship. But where he died and had unallocated funds that are allocated for gift offerings, which deals with [a case where] he separated coins and said, "These coins are for the offerings of my naziriteship," he would not be able to bring a single offering with all of them, for he said "offerings" [in the plural]; therefore, there is money for a sin-offering in these coins. Therefore, [the Gemara] objects: How could all of them be [used for] a gift offering, when money for a sin-offering is mingled with them? And through this, the phrasing of the Mishnah in Meilah (11a) is settled: "One who separates [money] for naziriteship, the laws of me'ilah do not apply to them, because they are fit to come entirely as peace-offerings" [and our Mishnah is dealing with this case]; and after that it teaches: "If he died and had unallocated funds..." But weren't we [already] dealing with unallocated funds? And so it should have said: "If he died, they are allocated for gift offerings" [without repeating "and had unallocated funds"]! Rather, here [in the first clause, the Mishnah is dealing with a case] where he said specifically "for my naziriteship," for then he can bring one of his offerings with all of them, as it implies that he meant any of his offerings; and therefore it teaches in the latter clause: "If he died and had unallocated funds" — [teaching that] even if he said, "These are for the offerings of my naziriteship," they all are allocated for gift offerings. And so it is proven from that [statement of Rava] below (26b): "[If one said:] 'These are for my sin-offering, and the remainder is for the rest of my naziriteship,' and he died, the money for the sin-offering shall go to the Dead Sea, and with the remainder he shall bring half as a burnt-offering and half as a peace-offering." And this implies that it is because he said "the remainder is for the rest of my naziriteship" that we consider him as one who says "for the offerings of my naziriteship"; but had he said "and the remainder is for my naziriteship" and not "for the rest," he could make all of them a burnt-offering or all of them a peace-offering from all of them. So explained Rabbeinu Yitzchak. [End of gloss].

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:2:1.hebrew: [האמרת] - ל"ג "תנן", דהוי משמע כאילו בא להקשות, והוא לא בא אלא לפרש. ו"הא אמרינן: מה שקנתה אשה קנה בעלה" — לאו דווקא, אלא כלומר: הכי קיימא לן בעלמא:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:2:1.english: ["Haven't you said"] - We do not read "we learned [in a Mishnah]," as that would imply that [the Gemara] comes to raise a difficulty, whereas it comes only to clarify. And [the phrasing] "But didn't we say: Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires" is not exact, but rather means: this is what is established for us in general.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:2:2.hebrew: שקימצה מעיסתה - וא"ת: והא אמר בפרק אע"פ (כתובות נט.) דמותר מזונות לבעל? וי"ל: דהכא מיירי שאמר לה: "צאי מעשה ידיך במזונותיך", ונתרצת בכך, והותירה ממעשה ידיה, והא ודאי דידה הוא. ועוד תירץ הר"ם: דהא דאמרינן "מותר מזונות לבעל" — כגון שקצבו לה כך וכך דינרין לשבת, והוזלו המזונות, שדי לה באותה קצבה כדי שבעה, והותר — אותו מותר לבעל; אבל הכא מיירי שקימצה מעיסתה, שלא הוזלו המזונות, אלא קימצה ופיחתה מפיה, שלא אכלה כדי שובע — דההוא מותר הוי ודאי דידה:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:2:2.english: Where she saved from her dough - And if you say: But doesn’t [the Gemara] say in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 59a) that the surplus of sustenance belongs to the husband? And it can be answered: Here it is dealing with [a case] where he said to her, “Go, [take] your earnings for your sustenance,” and she consented to this, and she had a surplus from her earnings, and this certainly belongs to her. And furthermore, the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir] answered: That which we say, “the surplus of sustenance belongs to the husband,” is, for example, where they allocated for her such-and-such dinars for the week and food prices dropped, so that that allocation was sufficient for her [to eat] to satiety and there was a surplus — that surplus belongs to the husband. But here it is dealing with [a case] where she saved from her dough, where food prices did not drop; rather, she economized and withheld from her mouth, for she did not eat to satiety — for that surplus certainly belongs to her.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:2:3.hebrew: ואמר לה על מנת שאין לבעליך רשות בהן - ר"ת פסק כרב, דאמר פרק בתרא דנדרים (דף פח.): המודר הנאה מחתנו ורוצה ליתן מעות לבתו, אומר: "הרי מעות נתונים ליך במתנה, ובלבד שלא יהא לבעליך רשות בהן, אלא מה שאת נושאת ונותנת בפיך". ואמר רב עלה: ל"ש אלא מה שאת נושאת ונותנת לתוך פיך, אבל אמר לה: "מה שתרצי תעשי" — קנה יתהון בעל. ואע"ג דשמואל פליג עליה התם, והלכתא כוותיה בדיני — מ"מ כי איתשיל, לענין איסורין איתשיל. ובשמעתין קיצר הש"ס, וי"ל שאמר לה: "מה שאת נושאת ונותנת לפיך":
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:2:3.english: "And he said to her: 'On condition that your husband has no rights to them'" - Rabbeinu Tam ruled in accordance with Rav, who said in the last chapter of Nedarim (88a): "[Regarding] one whose son-in-law is prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from him, and he wishes to give money to his daughter, he says: 'This money is hereby given to you as a gift, provided that your husband shall have no rights to it, except for what you take and put into your mouth.'" And Rav said concerning it: They taught [this] only [where he said]: "What you take and put into your mouth"; but if he said to her: "Do whatever you wish," the husband acquires them. And even though Shmuel disagrees with him there, and the halakha follows him [Shmuel] in monetary matters, nevertheless, when [this question] was asked, it was asked concerning a matter of [ritual] prohibitions. And in our sugya, the Talmud was concise, and it can be said that he said to her: "What you take and put into your mouth."

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:3:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל לאבוה בר איהי לא תיתיב - אלא עמוד על כרעיך — על רגליך, כמו "מתותי כרעיה דר' חנינא" בפרק קמא דחולין (דף ז:) — עד דאמרת לי הדא מלתא:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:3:1.english: Shmuel said to Avuh bar Ihi: "Do not sit" - Rather, stand on your feet — [meaning] on your legs, as in: "from under the feet of Rabbi Chanina" in the first chapter of Chullin (7b) — until you tell me this matter.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:3:2.hebrew: אלו הן אילים שלו ושלה ושל אחר מיתה ושל אחר כפרה - אע"ג דכולן משניות הם, שמא שלאחר כפרה, דלא תנינא בהדיא, קמיבעיא ליה. אי נמי: כל זה מדברי שמואל — "שלה הא דאמרן" עד [דפריך] ליה: "ותו ליכא? והא איכא ושאר שלמי נזיר" — כל זה פריך שמואל לאבוה בר איהי, והשיב: "שלא כמצותן לא קחשיב":
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:3:2.english: "These are the rams: His, hers, and that of after death, and that of after atonement" - Even though all of them are [taught in] Mishnayot, perhaps [the case of the ram brought] after atonement, which we have not learned explicitly [in a Mishnah], was what he was asking him. Alternatively, all of this is from the words of Shmuel: [from] "Hers — that which we said" until [the point where] he challenged him, "And are there no more? But isn't there [the case of] other peace-offerings of a nazirite?!" — all this Shmuel posed as a challenge to Avuh bar Ihi, and he replied: "[Those slaughtered] not according to their commandment are not counted."

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:4:1.hebrew: שלה הא דאמרן - במתני' (היינו בממונה):
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:4:1.english: "Hers — this is that which we said" - [This was stated] in the Mishnah (that is, with her [own] money).

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:4:2.hebrew: שלו דתנן האיש מדיר בנו בנזיר - מתני' היא בפירקין (לקמן נזיר כח:), ובשילהי פירקין מפרש ליה: למר — דהלכה היא דאיש מדיר בנו, [והלכה] נתקבל דיכול למחות, בין הוא בין קרוביו; לפיכך, גלח הוא ועשה מעשה בגופו לבטל נזירות אביו, או שמיחה בדיבורו:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:4:2.english: "His, as we learned: A man can vow his son to become a nazirite" - This is a mishna in our chapter (below, Nazir 28b), and at the end of our chapter [the Gemara] explains it: according to the Master [Rabbi Yoḥanan], it is a halakhah [transmitted to Moses from Sinai] that a man can vow his son to become a nazirite, and [as a halakhah] it was received that he is able to object, whether he [himself] or his relatives; therefore, [the mishna mentions whether] he shaved and performed an action upon his body to cancel his father's naziriteship, or he objected in speech.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:6:1.hebrew: שלאחר מיתה - "דתנן" גרסינן, דמשנה היא פ"ג דמעילה (דף יא.): "המפריש מעות לנזירותו לא נהנין ולא מועלין". לא נהנין — מדרבנן, או שמא אפילו מדאורייתא אסור, אע"ג דקיימא לשלמים, מידי דהוה אשלמים מחיים — דנהי דמעילה ליכא, איסור דאורייתא איכא:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:6:1.english: That is after death - We read "As we learned in a Mishnah" [detnan], as it is a Mishnah in chapter 3 of Me'ilah (11a): "One who designates money for his naziriteship, one may not derive benefit [from it] and is not liable for misuse [me'ilah]." [Is] "one may not derive benefit" [only] by rabbinic law, or perhaps it is forbidden even by Torah law, even though [the money] stands for peace-offerings, just as is the case with peace-offerings while [the animal is] alive — for granted that there is no [liability for] misuse, there is a Torah prohibition?

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:6:2.hebrew: מפני שראוין כולם לבא שלמים - דכיון שלא פירש כלום, אם [יתרמי לו בהמה] שמינה, יביא בכולן שלמים אם ירצה, והשאר יביא מביתו; ולכך אין מועלין בהן:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:6:2.english: "Because they are all fit to be brought as peace-offerings" - For since he did not specify anything, if a fat animal presents itself to him, he may bring peace-offerings with all of [the money] if he wishes, and the rest he will bring from his house; and therefore, [the laws of] misuse of consecrated property do not apply to them.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:7:1.english: "[If] he had unallocated funds, they shall fall to a gift-offering" - A communal gift-offering is a burnt-offering.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:7:2.hebrew: ואין טעונין לחם - במנחות (דף ד: ד"ה ואין) פרשינן, דבעי על כפי נזיר לתנופה, וליכא:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:7:2.english: "And they do not require bread" - In Menachot (4b, s.v. Ve'ein), we explained that [the bread] requires [placement] upon the hands of the nazirite for waving, and [here] there is none.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:8:1.hebrew: שלאחר מיתה מאי טעמא - לא בעי שלמים לחם, דלא חזיא לכפרה, ואין כאן כפי נזיר. שלאחר כפרה נמי — כגון שנדר והפריש קרבנותיו ואבדו, והביא אחרים ונתכפר בהן, ואח"כ נמצאו הראשונים — אותן שלמים נמי קריבין בלא לחם:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:8:1.english: "What is the reason [for an offering sacrificed] after death?" - The peace-offering does not require bread because it is not fit for atonement, and there are no hands of a nazirite here [for the waving]. [With regard to an offering sacrificed] after atonement as well — such as where one vowed [a nazirite vow] and designated his offerings, and they were lost, and he brought others and achieved atonement through them, and afterward the first [offerings] were found — that peace-offering, too, is sacrificed without bread.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:9:1.hebrew: ותו ליכא והאיכא ושאר שלמי נזיר ששחטן שלא כמצותן - פירש רש"י במנחות (דף מח:): ששחטן שלא לשמן. עוד פירש שם לישנא אחרינא: "שלא כמצותן" — דאיל כתיב ביה בן שתי שנים, והביאם בני שנה; [כשרים] לשלמי נדבה:
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:9:1.english: "And is there nothing else? But isn’t there: And other peace-offerings of a nazirite that were slaughtered not in accordance with their mitzva" - Rashi explained in Menachot (48b) that he slaughtered them not for their sake [shelo lishmam]. He also explained there an alternative explanation: "Not in accordance with their mitzva" — for regarding a ram, it is written of it [that it must be] two years old, yet he brought them [as animals] in their first year; [they are fit] as voluntary peace-offerings.

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:9:2.hebrew: ונאכלין ליום אחד - כחומר שלמי נזיר, דשאר שלמים נאכלין לשני ימים; דדינן כתודה, דאמר מר: "על זבח תודת שלמיו" — לרבות שלמי נזיר (מנחות דף יט.):
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:9:2.english: "And they are eaten for one day" - [This is] in accordance with the stringency of a nazirite’s peace-offering, for other peace-offerings are eaten for two days; for their law is like [that of] a thanksgiving-offering, as the Master stated: "Upon the sacrifice of the thanksgiving of his peace-offerings" — to include the peace-offering of a nazirite (Menachot 19a).

Tosafot on Nazir 24b:9:3.hebrew: ואין טעונין לא לחם ולא זרוע - הואיל ואין הנזיר ניתר בהן, לכך אין טעונין זרוע להתבשל עם האיל ולעשות תנופה. וה"ה דבמתניתין הוה ליה למיתני: "ולא זרוע":
Tosafot on Nazir 24b:9:3.english: "And they require neither bread nor the foreleg" - Since the nazirite is not permitted [to drink wine] through them, therefore they do not require the foreleg to be cooked with the ram and to perform the waving. And the same applies to our Mishnah: it should have taught: "nor the foreleg."
